subject: physics_2
question_text: Define power factor. On which factors does power factor depend?

verification.note: The 1+1 mark split is INVENTED and is a CLAIM until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it. For this Physics-II paper the two-book union check and the past-paper back-test are STRUCTURALLY IMPOSSIBLE — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material on hand is first-year physics only, and the paper corpus holds only Paper-I papers. Physics hand-checked: cos φ = R/Z from the impedance triangle (R adjacent to φ, Z the hypotenuse), so the two printed definitions — cosine of the phase angle, and ratio of resistance to impedance — are the same statement; Z = √(R² + (ωL − 1/ωC)²) carries ω, so the power factor depends on R, Z and through Z on the supply frequency, as the book notes.

recall_prompt: Say the steps you would write for this answer, in order. You can speak in English, in Telugu, or in both.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The definition
lines: The power factor of an a.c. circuit is the
cosine of the phase angle φ between the

lines.text: power factor = cos φ = R / Z

lines: It is also the ratio of the resistance R
steps.margin_note: First mark. Either definition earns it; write both — they are the same statement.
steps.why: Both printed definitions are one statement: in the impedance triangle R is the side along the current and Z the longest side, so cos φ is exactly R/Z.
common_mistakes: Defining it as the sine of the phase angle. The power factor is the cosine.
Writing Z/R. The power factor is R over Z, and it can never be more than 1.

recall.must_convey: That the power factor is the cosine of the phase angle between the voltage and the current, equal to R/Z.

steps.memory_tip: Power factor = cos φ = R/Z — cosine, and R on top.

steps.label: What it depends on
lines: It depends on the resistance R and the
Z changes with the supply frequency, so the
power factor also changes with the frequency.
steps.margin_note: Second mark. Name R and Z, then add that Z depends on the frequency.
steps.why: Naming R and Z answers the asked question; adding that Z depends on frequency shows why the same circuit can have different power factors on different supplies.
common_mistakes: Stopping at R and Z without noting that Z, and so the power factor, changes with the frequency.

recall.must_convey: That the power factor depends on the resistance and the impedance, and through Z on the supply frequency.

steps.memory_tip: Two letters in the formula, two factors it depends on: R and Z.

insider_note: The book's own answer adds that Z depends on frequency after naming R and Z — include that line, it is the second half of the asked question.
